description: Patterns and named venues to flag with avoidFlag=true. These dilute or backfire at EB-1A final merits. Match venue names/domains against these on ingest; when matched, set avoidFlag=true and surface a warning.

patterns.signal: pay-to-publish / pure APC with no real review
patterns.why: USCIS views pay-to-play outlets as weak evidence; MDPI-style stigma noted by counsel.
examples: outlets with no named editorial review process

patterns.signal: sells judge/mentor seats or lets anyone self-register as a judge
patterns.why: The judging memo warns these undermine the independent-selection requirement and can be cited negatively.
examples: any program charging a fee to be listed as a judge

patterns.why: Rarely move the needle for a seasoned professional; usable only sparingly as supporting evidence.
examples: student poster sessions presented as judging

patterns.why: Lower evidentiary weight; counsel has seen mixed USCIS treatment.
examples: Hacker Noon (noted as tougher for EB-1A; has worked for O-1A)

notDisqualifying: Avoid-flagged items are not deleted; they stay visible with a warning and are excluded from counted coverage. The owner can override a flag per venue.
